input: Write a short op-ed for the community newsletter

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The topic or issue the op-ed addresses completely determines the content, argument, and research needed — without it, nothing can be written.
Knowing who the intended readers are (e.g., a local neighbourhood, a school community, a professional association) shapes the assumed knowledge level, tone, and relevance of examples used.
A word or character limit set by the newsletter dictates how much argument and evidence can be developed — 200 words vs. 600 words are very different pieces.
The desired tone — passionate and rallying, calm and reasoned, humorous, urgent — fundamentally changes how the argument is constructed and voiced.
Whether this is a recurring newsletter, a special issue, or tied to a recent local event affects framing, urgency, and timeliness of the piece.
Knowing what the op-ed should achieve — raise awareness, prompt action, start a conversation, persuade a decision-maker — determines the structure and call to action.
Whether the user wants a ready-to-submit draft, a rough outline to iterate on, or just a strong opening paragraph determines how much to produce right now.

gold.taskTitle: Write a short op-ed for the community newsletter
gold.taskDescription: Draft a short opinion piece intended for publication in a community newsletter.

questions.title: What specific topic or issue should the op-ed argue?
questions.description: Identify the central subject and the position or angle the op-ed will take on it.

questions.title: Who are the readers of this newsletter?
questions.description: Define the community audience — e.g., a local neighbourhood, school families, a civic association — to calibrate assumed knowledge and relevance.

questions.title: Is there a word count limit from the newsletter?
questions.description: Determine whether a specific length is required or expected by the publication.

questions.title: What tone should the piece carry?
questions.description: Establish whether the op-ed should feel urgent, conversational, passionate, measured, or something else entirely.

questions.title: Is the op-ed tied to a recent local event or moment?
questions.description: Understand whether there is a specific trigger, deadline, or timely context that should be referenced or addressed.

questions.title: What should readers think, feel, or do after reading it?
questions.description: Clarify the intended outcome — e.g., sign a petition, attend a meeting, simply reconsider a viewpoint — to shape the call to action.

questions.title: Do you want a full draft or an outline to start?
questions.description: Determine the immediate deliverable so the right level of output is produced in the next step.
